brief: Indirect US-Iran talks in Doha entered a third day, with Qatar seeking release of over $6bn in Iranian assets that could help reopen the Strait of Hormuz.
Opposition-led protests in Delhi over the removal of 130 million names from India's voter roll drew tens of thousands.
A judge ordered the Trump administration to stop threatening US election officials who were sent letters seeking to set aside ballots of possible non-citizen voters.
Cost-of-living protests across Europe turned violent in several places, with a France investigation, looting in Germany and clashes in Portugal and Switzerland reported.

stories.headline: Gulf negotiators brace for US response to Iranian proposal on reopening Hormuz
stories.summary: Indirect talks in Doha entered a third day as Qatar tries to negotiate the release of more than $6bn in Iranian assets. Officials from Gulf states are reportedly "braced for the worst" while awaiting Washington's response to an Iranian proposal that could reopen the strait of Hormuz before the US midterm elections.
stories.whyItMatters: The strait of Hormuz is a major shipping route, and the talks could also affect the restart of negotiations on Iran's nuclear programme.
stories.rationale: Major geopolitical development with credible Guardian reporting, though the excerpt is partial and the outcome is unresolved.

stories.headline: Tens of thousands protest in Delhi over voter roll removals
stories.summary: Thousands of opposition supporters, led by the Congress party, gathered in Delhi to protest the Modi government. The protests are driven by anger over a large-scale revision of the voter roll that the report says erased 130 million names.
stories.whyItMatters: The voter roll dispute touches on electoral participation and public trust in a national election process affecting a very large population.
stories.rationale: Large-scale political protest on a consequential electoral issue, reported by the Guardian.

stories.headline: Judge orders Trump administration to stop threatening election officials
stories.summary: A judge ordered the Trump administration to stop threatening US election officials. The order follows letters that demanded officials set aside ballots of possible non-citizen voters.
stories.whyItMatters: The ruling addresses federal pressure on local election administration ahead of the midterms.
stories.rationale: Consequential legal development on election administration, reported by the BBC; the excerpt is brief, so details beyond the order are not available.

stories.headline: Cost-of-living protests across Europe turn violent in several countries
stories.summary: Protests over the cost of living spread across Europe, with more than 320,000 people reported to have demonstrated across France. In Germany, shops were looted in cities including Berlin, Hamburg and Frankfurt, and French officials opened an attempted murder investigation after a petrol bomb was thrown at riot police. Police cleared camps in Portugal and security forces in Switzerland were attacked with paving stones.
stories.whyItMatters: The demonstrations span several countries and reflect broad public anger over living costs and public services, with police and officials responding to clashes.
stories.rationale: Combines three candidate reports of the same European protest wave to avoid duplicate coverage; each source is attributed and some excerpts are partial.

stories.headline: Spanish train collision near Urda kills at least 69, including Cambridge scientist
stories.summary: A train collision near Urda in Toledo province, Spain, on Wednesday killed at least 69 people, according to the Guardian. Among the dead was Dr Marta Shahbazi, 41, a Cambridge Stem Cell Institute affiliate and Medical Research Council group leader, who was travelling to a conference.
stories.whyItMatters: The crash is a major loss of life, and the Cambridge link brings attention to the human toll among the victims.
stories.rationale: A high-casualty transport disaster; the excerpt does not cover the cause or investigation, so those details are omitted.
